name: Titusville drilled oil production
description: A mechanically drilled oil well at Titusville became a documented episode in commercial petroleum development in Pennsylvania.

places.note: Present-day country or region reference; ancient political boundaries are not implied.

date.basis: The cited source dates the episode.

events.statement: Edwin Drake led drilling of an oil-producing well near Titusville, Pennsylvania, in 1859.
events.caveats: The source calls this the world’s first oil well; oil extraction and drilling elsewhere preceded it, so that priority claim is not used.

evidence.supports: NPS identifies Drake’s role, place, year and oil discovery.

contributions.resource: Directed the drilling as chief engineer

evidence.supports: The nomination describes Drake’s role as chief engineer in charge of oil production.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest episode established by the cited evidence for this precisely scoped record; not a claim of global origin.

caveats: The date and depth are from a retrospective nomination. The well is not presented as the first extraction of petroleum or first drilled well globally.

measures.subject: Drake well at Titusville
measures.conditions: Depth reported by NPS for August 1859; not total regional production.

research.note: Initial evidence-backed admission; classifications and historical interpretations await independent review. Independent review checked cited event dates, wording and, where marked, numerical measures; other facets retain their original status.
